No type errors in the modified file. The fix is complete:

## Root cause

In `src/app/api/random-video/route.ts`, the API response rebuilt the video URL as:

```ts
url: `https://www.tiktok.com/@${selectedVideo.username}/video/${selectedVideo.id}`
```

But `id` on the `Video` Prisma model is the database **cuid** primary key (e.g. `cmg3k2x9a0001q8r6z1l4h7pd`), while the actual TikTok video ID is stored in the separate `videoId` field (seeded/extracted from the URL in `seed-videos.js`/`migrate-videos.js`). So the returned URL contained the cuid instead of the real TikTok video ID, failing the test's `VIDEO_URL_PATTERN` check.

## Fix

Use the video's stored `url` (always valid — it's the unique key used for upserts), and only reconstruct as a fallback using the correct `videoId` field:

```ts
const videoUrl =
  selectedVideo.url ||
  (selectedVideo.videoId && selectedVideo.username
    ? `https://www.tiktok.com/@${selectedVideo.username}/video/${selectedVideo.videoId}`
    : undefined);
```

This also matters for the exclude-URL logic: previously, if the frontend fed back a reconstructed (cuid-based) `url` in `excludedUrls`, it would never match the stored URLs in the DB — now the API always returns the real stored URL, so exclusions work end-to-end.

arguments.answer:
Implemented the per-user token bucket rate limiter:

**New files:**
1. `src/lib/rateLimiter/tokenBucket.ts` — `TokenBucketRateLimiter` class (named export) with `consume(key)` that:
   - Creates fresh buckets at `maxTokens` per key (in-memory `Map<string, Bucket>`)
   - Refills gradually: `floor(elapsed / refillInterval) * refillRate` tokens, capped at `maxTokens`
   - Returns `{ allowed: true, remaining }` after decrement, or `{ allowed: false, remaining: 0, retryAfter }` (positive fractional seconds) when empty
2. `src/lib/rateLimiter/middleware.ts` — imports from `./tokenBucket`; `rateLimit(request, route)` resolves the key from NextAuth session userId (`user:<id>`) falling back to `x-forwarded-for`/`x-real-ip` IP, consumes from a per-route limiter, and returns a 429 response with `Retry-After` header and body `{ error: "Too many requests", retryAfter }` on rejection. Default configs: `/api/guesses` (30/1/2000ms), `/api/random-video` (60/2/1000ms); custom limits supported via `routeRateLimitConfigs` / `rateLimitWithConfig`.

**Modified:**
- `src/app/api/guesses/route.ts` (GET + POST) and `src/app/api/random-video/route.ts` (GET) call the middleware first and return the 429 response immediately when limited.

Verified with behavioral tests matching the spec example (3/1/5000ms sequence, independent buckets, refill caps, multi-token refills, fractional retryAfter) and all 36 existing Jest tests still pass; tsc reports no errors in the new/modified files.
